mission.title: Install and Configure VMware Tanzu Kubernetes Grid
mission.description: VMware Tanzu Kubernetes Grid is a distribution that provides a robust platform for deploying and managing Kubernetes clusters in an enterprise environment. It leverages the Tanzu Framework and Carvel packaging to enhance integration and usability. Key trade-offs include the complexity of setup and the need for familiarity with VMware tools.

steps.title: Install the Tanzu CLI
steps.description:
This step installs the Tanzu CLI, which is essential for managing Tanzu Kubernetes Grid clusters.

```bash

curl -L https://github.com/vmware-tanzu/tanzu-framework/releases/download/v0.29.0/tanzu-framework-linux-amd64.tar.gz | tar xz -C /usr/local/bin

```

> This command downloads and extracts the Tanzu CLI to /usr/local/bin.

steps.title: Initialize the Tanzu CLI
steps.description:
This step initializes the Tanzu CLI and sets up the necessary configuration.

```bash

tanzu init

```

> This command initializes the Tanzu CLI and prepares it for use.

steps.title: Create a Tanzu Kubernetes Cluster
steps.description:
This step creates a new Tanzu Kubernetes cluster with specified Kubernetes version and node count.

```bash

tanzu cluster create my-cluster --kubernetes-version v1.29.0 --plan dev --workers 3

```

> This command creates a cluster named 'my-cluster' with 3 worker nodes.
commands: tanzu cluster create my-cluster --kubernetes-version v1.29.0 --plan dev --workers 3

steps.title: Configure Kubeconfig
steps.description:
This step configures the kubeconfig file to access the newly created cluster.

```bash

tanzu cluster kubeconfig get my-cluster --admin --context

```

> This command retrieves the kubeconfig for the 'my-cluster' cluster.

steps.title: Verify Cluster Nodes
steps.description:
This step verifies that the nodes in the cluster are up and running.

```bash

kubectl get nodes

```

> This command lists all nodes in the cluster and their statuses.

uninstall.title: Delete the Tanzu Kubernetes Cluster
uninstall.description:
This step removes the Tanzu Kubernetes cluster and all associated resources. Data loss may occur.

```bash

tanzu cluster delete my-cluster

```

> This command deletes the 'my-cluster' cluster.

uninstall.title: Clean Up Orphaned Resources
uninstall.description:
This step ensures that any orphaned resources such as load balancers and PVCs are removed.

```bash

kubectl delete pvc --all

```

> This command deletes all persistent volume claims in the current namespace.

upgrade.title: Upgrade the Tanzu Kubernetes Cluster
upgrade.description:
Backup the current cluster, upgrade the cluster, and verify the upgrade.

```bash

tanzu cluster backup my-cluster

tanzu cluster upgrade my-cluster --kubernetes-version v1.29.1

kubectl get nodes

```

> This command creates a backup of the 'my-cluster' cluster.
> This command upgrades the cluster to Kubernetes version 1.29.1.
> This command verifies that the nodes are running the new version.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Failed to create cluster: timeout waiting for cluster to be ready'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The cluster may not have enough resources allocated or there may be network issues.

**Fix:**
Check resource allocation and ensure network connectivity to the cluster.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'kubectl: command not found'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The kubectl CLI is not installed or not in the PATH.

**Fix:**
Install kubectl using 'curl -LO https://storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-release/release/$(curl -s https://storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-release/release/stable.txt)/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl && chmod +x ./kubectl && sudo mv ./kubectl /usr/local/bin/kubectl'

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Insufficient permissions to access the cluster'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The kubeconfig context may not have the necessary permissions.

**Fix:**
Ensure the kubeconfig is set correctly and the user has the required permissions.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Cluster not found'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The specified cluster name may be incorrect or the cluster may not exist.

**Fix:**
Verify the cluster name and check if it exists using 'tanzu cluster list'.

versionNotes.changes: Added support for Kubernetes 1.29, improved integration with Carvel tools.
versionNotes.migrationSteps: If upgrading from 2.4, ensure to back up existing clusters and review the new Carvel integration documentation.

resolution.summary: You should see the output of 'kubectl get nodes' listing all nodes in the 'Ready' state.
